mainEntity.name: What is an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) and how does it relate to a guest house?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) is a secondary housing unit on a single-family residential lot. While a guest house typically implies a non-rental dwelling for visitors, an ADU specifically refers to a legally permitted, independent living space that can be rented out or used by family members. Building a guest house often falls under ADU regulations in areas like Alameda and Berkeley, offering benefits such as increased property value or potential rental income. Understanding local zoning is a critical first step to determine if your guest house project qualifies as an ADU and what specific requirements apply.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a legally permitted, secondary housing unit on a residential lot, which a guest house can often qualify as, particularly in areas like Alameda and Berkeley. It allows for independent living and can offer rental income or increased property value.
